entries.summary: Conservative author and commentator (2,135,066 followers) quoted a viral clip post of the Nov. 20 White House briefing and wrote: “Instead of the JD/Rubio debate over our next presidential candidate, let’s make it The People’s Choice, Stephen Miller.” The quoted post, by @jenrenee (41,185 followers, below the 50,000 threshold), said “I clapped in my kitchen. Miller is fantastic” and showed President Trump, after Miller spoke at the podium, telling reporters “He was better than these two guys” (Vance and Rubio) and asking Miller, “Do you want to run for president?” On Nov. 22 at 4:03 PM PT, Coulter followed up without naming Vance: “My idea for Trump: golf for two years, meet world leaders, take photo ops, and leave Washington to Stephen Miller. Miller just pulled Mullin off TV after his DACA comments. Forgiven for breaking the law? That’s amnesty. Stop BSing us.” (4,142 likes, 610 reposts, 252 replies, 124,707 views). She also said on The Clay & Buck Show, as reported by The Daily Beast on Nov. 22, that she does not expect “a groundswell of support for Rubio.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created September 2010 (2,135,066 followers, 2,081 following, 93,721 posts, blue verified). The 25 replies and 25 quote/related posts opened were unique text, mostly arguing Miller would be unelectable or a “gift to Democrats,” with a minority agreeing; no copy-paste flood.

Cupp (@secupp, 428,655), CNN and New York Daily News commentator, quoted it: “No, but I love that this sentiment still exists. It’s like the flat earthers and the people who believe Avril Lavigne is a body double and Stevie Wonder can see. It’s so dumb, it’s funny” (878 likes, 33,900 views). Jenna Ellis (@realJennaEllis, 1,132,322), senior policy adviser at the American Family Association and AFR radio host (per bio), a former Trump 2020 campaign legal adviser, quoted it: “Let’s really not. Some people have learned literally nothing during the Trump era and it shows” (70 likes, 9,431 views). Jon Cooper (@joncoopertweets, 1,372,161) posted a separate item, logged below. None of those three was added to the opposition list: they were criticizing Coulter’s Miller pick, not Vance. entries.summary: News report on President Trump’s Nov. 21, 2026 interview with Kayleigh McEnany on Fox News’s “Saturday in America.” Asked who he would like to see run in 2028, Trump said of the Republican side: “Obviously, JD’s vice president, Marco is right up there. The two of them are doing fantastically. They’re both very, very popular. But you could have some surprises. We have some very capable people.” Asked whether the GOP “should be an open primary with lots of robust debates, or there should be some sort of unity ticket that the party coalesces around,” Trump said “could be either,” then: “There could be some great unity tickets. I’ll tell you what, the unity tickets are fantastic. You save all that money, you use it against the Democrats. I think it could be either.” He also said that “in another few weeks, it’s going to be starting hot and heavy,” and that “we’ll be involved and we’ll be watching.” The article does not record him naming who would be president or vice president on such a ticket, or formally endorsing either man. This is a return to a theme he has raised before: at a May 11, 2026 Rose Garden dinner he called a Vance–Rubio pairing a “dream team” and “a perfect ticket” (Newsweek), and in a June 3, 2026 New York Post “Pod Force One” interview he said, “I like them both, and I like them together,” and “I don’t know how you beat them if they’re together. That would be a great team” (The Hill; Reuters quoted him as saying “I would think that JD and Marco as a team would be very hard to beat”). The @FoxNews post of today’s interview (29.5 million followers; 334 likes, 56 reposts, 79 replies, 11 quotes, 89,015 views at the time of this update) used the same “doing fantastically” line and a 51-second clip.

authenticity.evidence: News report on a televised interview. Quotes were checked against the Fox News article and against clip posts of the same interview on X (including @EricLDaugh and @FoxNews).

entries.audience_sample: The official @FoxNews post of the story (https://x.com/FoxNews/status/2124165345741041956) had modest engagement for a 29.5-million-follower account. Marco is right up there. The two of them are doing fantastically,” and, asked about an open primary versus “some sort of unity ticket,” “Could be either. There could be some great unity tickets. I’ll tell you what, unity tickets are fantastic. You save all that money, you use it against the Democrats.” Daugherty added that the two are in a “dead heat” at “Vance at 33.3% and Rubio at 32.6% in the national primary polling average,” recalled Trump’s May “dream team” line, and said the field “might just get packed.” Those 33.3 / 32.6 figures are his, not this tracker’s average (this site’s opened-poll average is Vance 33.9 / Rubio 31.6).

entries.theme: Iran war / 'forever war' / fitness for office
entries.summary: On his radio show Tuesday, Nov 17, Fox & Friends co-host Brian Kilmeade played Vance's Nov 16 Ingraham Angle answer that whatever Trump decides on Iran, 'there are going to be people who demand more, who want the war to go on indefinitely,' and that Trump 'is not going to let this become a forever war.' Kilmeade called that 'another straw man argument,' said 'there is not one person that I have ever met that wants an endless war,' and said of Vance: 'Never should have been vice president.' He also objected to Vance's post-midterm line that any honest conversation about the losses 'has to start with the Iran war.' Also reported by The Hill, TV Insider, HuffPost and The Daily Beast (opened). Kilmeade did not post the remarks on his own X account in this window; the follower count is his @kilmeade account.

entries.summary: In a thread asking which elected Republican besides Trump has the most “raw political talent” (charisma and “vibes,” not policy agreement), Walsh surveyed replies and posted a 24-hour poll of the four names that came up most: Vance, Rubio, Gill, and DeSantis. A later reply in the comments identified Gill as Rep. Brandon Gill. Final result (poll closed Nov 18, 2026, 11:13 AM PT; 67,220 votes): Rubio 31,794 (47.3%), DeSantis 19,338 (28.8%), Gill 8,635 (12.8%), Vance 7,453 (11.1%). Vance finished last. Walsh does not endorse or attack Vance in the thread; he includes him as one of the names mentioned. The original question post (8:21 AM PT, Nov 17) had 6,486 likes, 208 reposts, 228 quotes, 5,627 replies, 566 bookmarks and 3,021,996 views at close.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof; X poll votes are anonymous, so votes are judged only indirectly. (1) Vote shares were stable to the end: from the earlier snapshot (59,262 votes) to the close (67,220), the late 7,958 votes split Rubio 49.9%, DeSantis 26.8%, Gill 12.2%, Vance 11.2%, versus 46.9 / 29.0 / 12.9 / 11.1% before; no late surge for any name. The final order also matches a public count of names in the replies (Rubio 1,293, DeSantis 861, Gill 656, Vance 347, from @frontrunnershow, a 2-week-old 435-follower account, so treat as rough). (2) Sampled commenters look like real accounts: 106 unique authors across 101 replies and 23 quote-posts; median account age about 4.7 years for repliers; 3 of 83 repliers had under 10 followers, 2 had default avatars, 2 had digit-string handles, 10 were created in 2026; no copy-paste flood (the most repeated reply was just “Marco Rubio,” 4 times). (3) Traffic toward Rubio was driven by big quote-posts rather than anonymous accounts: Laura Loomer’s quote (“Marco Rubio… not even a contest”) reached 143,535 views, 8,930 likes and 814 reposts, and Pino Americano’s poll quote reached 23,610 views and 121 reposts. Caveat: among 62 sampled reposters of the Pino quote, 16 (26%) average more than 100 posts a day and 7 use default avatars, a pattern typical of high-volume retweet accounts; that is amplification, not evidence of vote stuffing.

entries.audience_sample: Quotes and replies opened leaned toward Rubio or DeSantis rather than Vance; in the sample, Rubio was named in 21 replies, DeSantis 14, Gill 9, Vance 4. Prominent commenters (50K+ followers or major-org tie), as fetched at close: Laura Loomer (@LauraLoomer, 1,935,729 followers; LOOMERED founder) replied “Marco Rubio” (2,403 likes, 39,175 views) and quoted the question: “Marco Rubio. And it’s not even a contest.” (8,930 likes, 814 reposts, 560 replies, 143,535 views) — pro-Rubio over Vance. Tomi Lahren (@TomiLahren, 2,865,491; OutKick/Fox News host) replied she wants someone who “stays true to the values and gets shit done,” naming DeSantis (2,245 likes, 180,478 views) — a preference, not a Vance critique; Walsh replied, “Yeah but that wasn’t my question.” Three Year Letterman (@3YearLetterman, 486,915; satire account) joked “Gerald Ford” (99 likes) — no stance. Kosher (@koshercockney, 183,833) quoted: “Wow. Nobody likes Vance.” (248 likes, 4,007 views) — critical. Pino Americano (@PinoAmericano, 117,273) quoted the poll: “JD Vance is nearly off the stage. Let’s go Rubio!” (1,187 likes, 121 reposts, 23,610 views) — critical. Walsh also posted a follow-up asking for non-politicians who could run in 2028 (1,737 likes, 682,381 views). Reply-to-like ratio on the poll post is 117%.
